dataset_id.identifier: To ensure that the data from this project are findable and accessible, they will be placed in open repositories. Data and metadata from this study will be registered in BioStudies and sample metadata described in BioSamples, as required by AQUASERV. The final processed chemical (mercury speciation and bioaccumulation), biomarker (protein quantification and enzymatic activity) and associated metadata will be published either in BioStudies repository as CSV files. Raw DNA sequencing data (FASTQ files) will be deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive (EMBL-ENA). Persistent identifiers are automatically created within the repositories to assign a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) to each dataset. The datasets will be made publicly available after publication of the associated scientific results.

dataset.description: This section will describe the types of datasets that will be generated from carrying out the in vivo microcosm exposures as outlined for the study MICROMIX - Interaction between microplastics and mercury in a benthic microcosm (PID 37027)

format:
This project will generate the following types of data:
  • General experimental metadata will be stored in spreadsheets (CSV/XLSX formats), for instance water quality parameters and time-points
  • Chemical data on mercury speciation (Hg2+ and CH3Hg) will be stored in spreadsheets (CSV and/or XLSX)
  • Bioaccumulation will be calculated from mercury speciation data, and stored as tabular datasets in spreadsheets (CSV and/or XLSX)
  • Biochemical data will include protein quantification and enzymatic activity measurements, stored in spreadsheets (CSV and XLSX)
  • Metagenomic data will include raw DNA sequencing reads (FASTQ), processed sequence data and taxonomic abundance tables (FASTA, TSV/CSV), together with associated bioinformatics outputs and metadata (TXT, CSV)

distribution.available_until: Yes. The data will be deposited in a repository as soon as possible after they are generated, but data and downstream analyses will remain under embargo until the corresponding manuscript is published, after which it will be made available.

dataset.description: This project involves in vivo exposure of aquatic invertebrates in a microcosm approach. The experiment will be conducted in controlled and enclosed facilities at Umeå Marine Sciences Centre, ensuring optimal conditions and minimisation of stress for improved animal welfare.  The project will follow the ethical principles and welfare standards to ensure high ethical standards in experimental design and animal care. This work will comply with the Swedish Animal Welfare Act and Ordinance as well as Umeå’s institutional guidelines for laboratory animal facilities and experimental biosafety.
dataset.title: Horizon Europe - Ethics

dmp.description:
Microplastics (MP) and mercury (Hg) are ubiquitous environmental pollutants with known adverse effects on organisms. In aquatic environments, their co-occurrence and properties promote interactions, which can alter the environmental fate, bioavailability and toxicity of both contaminants. This project aims to investigate the ecotoxicological impacts of MP-Hg interactions on benthic ecosystems through in vivo microcosm exposures of bivalves (Macoma balthica) in the presence of Hg-resistant microbial communities in the sediment. The objectives are to assess mercury speciation, bioaccumulation, toxicity biomarkers and gut microbiome. The expected outcomes are new insights on the interactions of MP-Hg and on their toxicological and ecological impact on benthic ecosystems. This data can contribute to the improvement of environmental risk assessment and management strategies.

This DMP describes the management of chemical speciation, biochemical and metagenomic data generated throughout the project. It ensures compliance with the FAIR principles and AQUASERV open access requirements.
dmp.title: Data Management Plan AQUASERV PID: 37027 MICROMIX - Interaction between microplastics and mercury in a benthic microcosm
